names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Παυσίλυπος ο εν Ηρακλεία της Θράκης αθλήσας», with the rank word and the clause naming where he contended left off. The page's own body adds a second form of the name, «(ή Παυσολύπιος)».
The alternative form saint.gr prints in the body of his page for 8 Απριλίου: «Ο Άγιος Μάρτυς Παυσίλυπος (ή Παυσολύπιος)».

Read out of the title on the name link behind his line for 8 апреля ст. ст., name page 1706, «Павсилип, мч.», with the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s own line gives the same form declined, «Павсилипа». The calendar gives him no see, no toponymic and no by-name — where the Greek line calls him «ο εν Ηρακλεία της Θράκης αθλήσας» — so the bare forename is the whole of the form it prints, and the «of Heraclea» in the display name is the corpus’s own off the Greek. No folder holds this form and none holds a form that folds with it; `.tmp/foldchk.py` and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` were both run before this draft.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 8 апреля ст. ст. — «Мч. Павсилипа (ок. 117-138).»

attestations.note: Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Απριλίου — «Άγιος Παυσίλυπος ο εν Ηρακλεία της Θράκης αθλήσας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It gives no year, only «στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Αδριανού (117-138 μ.Χ.)», and no `dates` were taken from a reign. The day's line puts his contest at Heraclea in Thrace; the page's body names only Rome, where he was born, and the eparch of Europe, Practus, and never names Heraclea, so `locations` were left out. The page prints no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).

death.note: **The folder carried no date at all before this.** days.pravoslavie.ru brackets «ок. 117-138» after his line for 8 апреля ст. ст., which is the reign of the emperor saint.gr names and dates 117 to 138 without turning it into a date of its own. A reign is a bound and not a date, so the interval is kept twenty-one years wide and the display says so; nothing in either page narrows it, neither gives a year of birth, and no new-style pair is constructed from anything here.
